response.sql:
WITH net_fees AS (
  SELECT f.orderslink, o.dealedge, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net_rate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink
  WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009
),
group_avgs AS (
  SELECT orderslink, dealedge,
         AVG(net_rate) AS group_avg_net,
         COUNT(net_rate) AS record_count
  FROM net_fees
  GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge
  HAVING COUNT(net_rate) > 0
),
side_avgs AS (
  SELECT orderslink, dealedge, group_avg_net, record_count,
         AVG(group_avg_net) OVER (PARTITION BY dealedge) AS side_avg
  FROM group_avgs
)
SELECT orderslink, dealedge AS side, group_avg_net, record_count,
       group_avg_net - side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg
FROM side_avgs
WHERE group_avg_net > side_avg
ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A fee record's net rate is feerate - rebrate, and any record where either value is NULL is excluded from the averages and counts (per 'ignoring missing values'). Fee records with feerate NULL are excluded by the > 0.0009 filter.
record_count counts only the records that contributed a non-NULL net rate, so it matches the population of the group average.
Each orderslink matches at most one orders row by recordvault. The schema does not declare recordvault as unique, so a duplicate would double-count fees in the join.
The side average is the unweighted mean of group averages across all (orderslink, side) groups for that side, computed after the fee-rate filter and the NULL exclusion.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat a missing rebrate as a zero rebate, so a fee record with a feerate but no rebrate still counts, with net rate equal to feerate.
alternatives.sql:
WITH net_fees AS (
  SELECT f.orderslink, o.dealedge, f.feerate - COALESCE(f.rebrate, 0) AS net_rate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink
  WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009
),
group_avgs AS (
  SELECT orderslink, dealedge,
         AVG(net_rate) AS group_avg_net,
         COUNT(net_rate) AS record_count
  FROM net_fees
  GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge
  HAVING COUNT(net_rate) > 0
),
side_avgs AS (
  SELECT orderslink, dealedge, group_avg_net, record_count,
         AVG(group_avg_net) OVER (PARTITION BY dealedge) AS side_avg
  FROM group_avgs
)
SELECT orderslink, dealedge AS side, group_avg_net, record_count,
       group_avg_net - side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg
FROM side_avgs
WHERE group_avg_net > side_avg
ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
